crossrefs.text: Be still before the LORD and wait patiently for Him; do not fret when men prosper in their ways, when they carry out wicked schemes.
Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways;
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue in the fear of the LORD.
Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?
But He gives us more grace. This is why it says: “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
Behold, the wicked man travails with evil; he conceives trouble and births falsehood.
His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and violence; trouble and malice are under his tongue.
The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, and debauchery;
Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
For we are Godʼs fellow workers; you are Godʼs field, Godʼs building.
Wisdom has built her house; she has carved out her seven pillars.
rooted and built up in Him, established in the faith as you were taught, and overflowing with thankfulness.
For lack of guidance, a nation falls, but with many counselors comes deliverance.
The house of the righteous has great treasure, but the income of the wicked is trouble.
Precious treasures and oil are in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish man consumes them.
Wisdom makes the wise man stronger than ten rulers in a city.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.
Let the wicked man forsake his own way and the unrighteous man his own thoughts; let him return to the LORD, that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will freely pardon.
We demolish arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God; and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
Mockers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
But Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?
Repent, therefore, of your wickedness, and pray to the Lord. Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart.
Then the Lordsaw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time.
A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary; His understanding is beyond searching out.
But those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.
So I ask you not to be discouraged because of my sufferings for you, which are your glory.

Do not let your heart grow faint, and do not be afraid when the rumor is heard in the land; for a rumor will come one year— and then another the next year— of violence in the land and of ruler against ruler.

David, however, said to himself, “One of these days now I will be swept away by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will stop searching for me all over Israel, and I will slip out of his hand.”
Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart.
And you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when He rebukes you.
Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.
For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul.
For surely there is a future, and your hope will not be cut off.
Your words were found, and I ate them. Your words became my joy and my heartʼs delight. For I bear Your name, O LORD God of Hosts.
But the one who looks intently into the perfect law of freedom, and continues to do so—not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer—he will be blessed in what he does.
They are more precious than gold, than much pure gold; they are sweeter than honey, than honey from the comb.
By them indeed Your servant is warned; in keeping them is great reward.
How sweet are Your words to my taste— sweeter than honey in my mouth!

I have come to my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice. I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; drink freely, O beloved.
Many are the afflictions of the righteous, but the LORD delivers him from them all.
Though he falls, he will not be overwhelmed, for the LORD is holding his hand.
Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will arise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
Then my enemy will see and will be covered with shame— she who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will see her; at that time she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
He will rescue you from six calamities; no harm will touch you in seven.
We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;
So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
But you should not gloat in that day, your brotherʼs day of misfortune, nor rejoice over the people of Judah in the day of their destruction, nor boast proudly in the day of their distress.
Do not fret over those who do evil; do not envy those who do wrong.
Depart from me, you evildoers, that I may obey the commandments of my God.
He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will be destroyed.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue in the fear of the LORD.
Do not envy wicked men or desire their company;
Everyone must submit himself to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which is from God. The authorities that exist have been appointed by God.
Pay everyone what you owe him: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.
Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, or set foot on the path of sinners, or sit in the seat of mockers.
Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
To show partiality is not good, yet a man will do wrong for a piece of bread.
A man takes joy in a fitting reply— and how good is a timely word!
Showing partiality to the wicked is not good, nor is depriving the innocent of justice.
So Pharaoh asked them, “Can we find anyone like this man, in whom the Spirit of God abides?”
And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was severe over all the earth.
The people will curse the hoarder of grain, but blessing will crown the one who sells it.
who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.
Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?
saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’
Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.
Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Make sure that no one repays evil for evil. Always pursue what is good for one another and for all people.
And the king commanded them to quarry large, costly stones to lay the foundation of the temple with dressed stones.
So Solomonʼs and Hiramʼs builders, along with the Gebalites, quarried the stone and prepared the timber and stone for the construction of the temple.
Allow no sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids.
and poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit.
So then, let us not sleep as the others do, but let us remain awake and sober.
But since we belong to the day, let us be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of our hope of salvation.
Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth.
Through laziness the roof caves in, and in the hands of the idle, the house leaks.
And do this, understanding the occasion. The hour has come for you to wake up from your slumber, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.

And to Adam He said: “Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life. Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you, and you will eat the plants of the field. By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread, until you return to the ground— because out of it were you taken. For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.”
